3. The plaintiffs' case, in short, is that the suit property originally belonged to C.S. recorded tenants Sree Luxmi Narayan and Rajendra Lal Sharma. Rajendra Lal Sharma died leaving behind only son Bholanath Sharma. The predecessor of the plaintiffs entered into the suit land at about 100 years ago and while living therein peacefully having uninterrupted possession he died on 16.7.1953 leaving behind the plaintiffs and their brother Ranjit Kumar Roy as legal heirs. Ranjit Kumar Roy, brother of the plaintiffs left the country before partition of the country. While the plaintiffs were living in the suit land they came to learn that one Zobeda Khatun purchased the suit land from Bholanath Sharma and she filed Title Suit No. 237 of 1960 for ejectment before the 6th court of Munsif Dhaka and the plaintiffs contested the suit by filing written statement and the said suit was dismissed. Zobeda Khatun did not claim the rent of the suit land thereafter and the plaintiffs did not admit her as the landlord. The so-called deed of sale in favour of Zobeda Khatun is false. Zobeda Khatun recorded her name in S.A. Khatian and mutated her name in the City Corporation but she never paid any tax. 

 5. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter-alia, that the suit land admittedly belonged to Rajendra Lal Sharma who constructed a building thereon in the year 1953 and enjoyed by letting out the same to tenants. Rajendra Lal Sharma died leaving behind his only heir Bholanath Sharma who mutated his name in the city Corporation and paid all taxes and the plaintiffs were the tenants under him. Thereafter Zobeda Khatun purchased the disputed land from Bholanath Sharma in 1954 by way of deed of sale and it was mentioned in the said deed that the plaintiffs were the tenants and they have right to recover the rent from the plaintiffs. Bholanath sold the disputed land after serving notices upon the plaintiffs to pay rent to Zobeda Khatun. Zobeda Khatun recorded her name in SA. Khatian and mutated her name with the city corporation and paid all taxes, Zobeda Khatun claimed rent from the plaintiffs several times but the plaintiffs did not pay the rent. Thereafter Zobeda Khatun filed a suit for ejectment against the plaintiffs and in the meantime the plaintiffs mutually agreed to vacate the suit land and accordingly Zobeda Khatun did not take any step and the said suit was dismissed for default. Zobeda Khatun sold the disputed land to the defendant no.1 and delivered physical possession to him. The defendant no. 1 having recorded his name in R.S. Khatian and mutated his name in the city corporation paid all taxes and thereafter sold the same to the defendant nos. 2 and 3 by two separate registered deeds of sale and delivered possession to them. The defendant nos. 2 and 3 claimed rent from the plaintiffs but the plaintiffs did not pay any rent and vacate the possession. The defendant nos. 2 and 3 served notices under section 106 of the T.P. Act upon the plaintiffs who replied to the said notices and thereafter the defendant nos. 2 and 3 filed a suit for ejectment before the Court of Assistant Judge and the same is pending for hearing. 

 8. We have heard Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 2 and Mrs. Sofia Khatun, the learned Advocate-On-Record appearing for the respondent No. 4, perused the leave petition, impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division and all other connected papers on record. It appears that one Zobeda Khatun purchased the disputed land from Bholanath Sharma in 1954 by a registered deed of sale wherein it was mentioned that the plaintiffs were tenants and Zobeda Khatun has right to recover rent from them Bholanath served notices upon the plaintiffs to pay rent to Zobeda Khatun who recorded her name in S.A. Khatian and mutated her name in the City Corporation and paid all taxes. Thereafter Zobeda Khatun claimed rent from the Plaintiffs several times but they did not pay rent. Thereafter the ejectment suit was filed against the plaintiffs but they agreed to vacate the suit land and consequently Zobeda Khatun sold the suit land to the defendant No.1 and delivered physical possession to him. The defendant No.1 recorded his name in H.S. Khatian and mutated his name in the City Corporation and thereafter he sold the same to defendant Nos. 2 and 3 by separate registered deeds of sale and delivered possession. The plaintiffs failed to pay rent and vacate the suit land. The defendants filed suit against the plaintiffs for ejectment which is pending for disposal. The High Court Division have held that both the courts below made concurrent findings of facts that the plaintiffs are tenants in the suit land and that the plaintiffs claim of title by way of adverse possession is hit by Section 116 of the Evidence Act and thus the plaintiffs failed to prove their title in the suit land; that Zobeda Khatun and the Government were necessary parties in the suit but they were not impleaded in the suit. The High Court Division have rightly found that both the courts below on proper appreciation of the evidence on record made concurrent findings of facts which should not be interfered with as there was no misreading or non-consideration of the material evidence on record.
